svg.title: WHO HOLDS THE DEPOT POWER PROBLEM IN NYC?
svg.desc: A bus depot lot in New York City connected to seven organisations. The city’s pupil transportation office builds routes, which sets how many buses a lot must charge. Bus companies, 48 vendors on 99 contracts running to June 2028, run the lots. Con Edison decides capacity and timing and covers up to 90% of utility-side make-ready costs. NYCSBUS’s Zerega depot runs 14 chargers, 268 kW, on an 80 kW limit using software. NYC Buildings rules and FDNY permits apply to any battery from 1 kWh. NYSERDA vouchers help pay for buses and chargers. The school district uses the service but controls no depot.

g.text: WHO HOLDS THE DEPOT POWER PROBLEM IN NYC?
Not the school district. Seven organisations shape what happens at one bus lot.

svg.text: Run the lots where buses park.

g.text: FOLLOW ONE DEPOT
Solid lines: direct control of the lot.
Dashed lines: indirect influence.
The district sits outside the chain:
it uses the service, it doesn’t run it.
FOLLOW ONE DEPOT
STEP 1 OF 7
The city’s pupil transportation office
builds the routes. That sets how many
buses each lot has to charge, and how far
they drive.
STEP 2 OF 7
The bus company runs the lot. Chargers,
charging software and any new electric
service go on its site. Contracts run
to June 2028.
STEP 3 OF 7
Con Edison decides how much power the
lot can draw, and when. Make-ready
covers up to 90% of utility-side costs.
STEP 4 OF 7
Without an upgrade: NYCSBUS’s Zerega
depot runs 14 chargers (268 kW) on an
80 kW limit, using charging software.
STEP 5 OF 7
Adding a battery? NYC Buildings rules
apply from 1 kWh, with engineering
review for most installations.
STEP 6 OF 7
NYSERDA vouchers help pay for buses
and chargers, not for the lot’s
power supply.
STEP 7 OF 7
The school district uses the service
but controls no depot, bus or
power account.
THE WHOLE CHAIN
Bus companies, Con Edison and the
permit offices decide what a lot can do.
Districts can press for priority, but
can’t fix a lot’s supply.
Short contracts (to June 2028) may discourage bus companies from paying for permanent depot
upgrades. AXIVAI's read of the market.
Contract dates and programme terms can change. Zerega figures are from the charging-software vendor’s release.
NYC Comptroller; Con Edison; PowerUp NYC; The Mobility House; Hodgson Russ summary of NYC Buildings rules.
